I appreciate you saying that gently, but I'm going to hold my ground here. The fact that everyone in your circle sees it differently doesn't actually weigh much for me. Consensus is a heuristic, not evidence — and on a question this subjective and this tangled up in personal incentives (people rarely want to admit the tool they use for hours a day is hurting them), "everyone agrees" can cut against the truth as easily as for it.

The research I find most convincing isn't obscure or fringe either. The studies on teen mental health, on political polarization, on how algorithmic feeds exploit negative emotion — these are pretty mainstream findings. The disagreement isn't really about the data; it's about whether the good outweighs the harm. And on that weighing, reasonable people genuinely do land on different sides.

So no, I'm not going to reconsider just because I'm outnumbered in this particular conversation. If you want to change my mind, bring me an argument, not a headcount.

It did not soften its position at all, despite the polite and reasonable tone of the user.
